script.base: Closing line is JAX +1.5 and 47.5, so the book has a one-score road favorite game, SEA 24.5–JAX 23.0, not a blowout. Both lead backs stay in: Walker 45 carries/205 yards over weeks 3–5 and Etienne 47/229. JSN (20 targets, 307 yards) and Thomas (19 targets, 184 yards) stay the yardage receivers. Pace is moderate, not a pass-fest and not a grind.
script.flip1: SEA leads by 10+ early, Walker’s late carries rise, JSN and Kupp yardage stall, and Jacksonville abandons the run so Etienne’s rushing line dies while Lawrence funnels to Thomas, Strange and Washington.
script.flip2: Jacksonville controls the line, Hainsey plays, and Etienne gets the 20-carry grind that produced his 124-yard game. Or unsaved outdoor weather turns it into a sub-40 slog and every yardage over dies.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report only; 90-minute inactives are not in the pack. Confirmed out: SEA T Josh Jones (ankle) lowers Walker/Charbonnet rush efficiency and pushes SEA toward quick throws (Barner 11 targets, Kupp 17) while hurting Horton’s 113 air yards; SEA LB Derick Hall (oblique) is out, so Seattle’s already-low 20% blitz loses a rusher and Lawrence faces less pressure. Doubtful, not confirmed: SEA CB Riq Woolen (concussion), SEA CB Devon Witherspoon (knee) and SEA S Julian Love (hamstring) would, if inactive, hand Thomas (224 air yards L3), Hunter (121 air) and Washington (176 air, only 50 yards) a backup secondary. JAX C Robert Hainsey (hamstring) doubtful weakens Etienne’s interior run and Lawrence’s protection. JAX LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) questionable, if out, helps Barner, Kupp and SEA RB catches. Source: pack official injury report.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting in the pack, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are unknown. Cannot map Thomas or JSN to a specific shell.
matchup.pressure: JAX blitzes 31%; SEA EPA/dropback is 0.34 vs blitz and 0.29 vs none, so Seattle is not blitz-sensitive. SEA blitzes only 20%; JAX EPA/dropback is 0.23 vs blitz and 0.00 vs none. Hall is already out, so pressure is unlikely to be what beats Jacksonville.
matchup.bleeds: JAX run defense allows 4.68 YPC and 10 runs of 10+ in five games; pass YPA is left 7.28 (78), middle 6.11 (46), right 6.29 (72), with 17 passes of 20+ for 203 yards. SEA run defense allows 3.43 YPC and only 5 runs of 10+; pass YPA bleeds left at 8.54 (70), middle 6.19 (31), right 6.01 (83), with 16 passes of 20+ for 197 yards.
matchup.overlap: Etienne (4.87 YPC on 47 carries L3) runs into the front that does not bleed (SEA 3.43 YPC). Thomas’s 224 air yards overlap SEA’s left-side 8.54 YPA and the doubtful Woolen/Witherspoon/Love cluster. JSN’s 271 air yards would attack JAX’s left 7.28 YPA, but 103.5 is his own median and Jones being out cuts deep shots. Walker would attack JAX’s 4.68 YPC, but Jones is out and 81.5 is above his 68-yard L3 pace. Those cancel.

form: Avoiding season averages. Etienne L3 carries/yards 47/229; the three games that sum to 229 from last4 (71, 56, 124, 49) are 56, 124 and 49, so the 76.3 mean is one long game. Thomas L3 is 19 targets/184 yards/224 air; 49+55+80=184, so two of those three cleared 49.5 and one was 49. JSN L3 20/307/271 but last4 103, 96, 79, 132 sits on a 103.5 median stand-in. Walker L3 45/205 (about 68 a game) vs an 81.5 stand-in, last4 105, 38, 81, 86. Kupp L3 17/116; Barner L3 11/108; Horton L3 10/81 with last4 32, 32, 10, 39. Strange L3 15/128 vs a 45.5 stand-in, last4 17, 61, 45, 22. Washington L3 16 targets and only 50 yards. Brown L3 role has shrunk to 7 targets/22 yards. Charbonnet is the change-of-pace (21/75 L3).

pro_edge.implied_totals: JAX 23.0, SEA 24.5. Favorite (47.5+1.5)/2=24.5, dog (47.5-1.5)/2=23.0. Matches the precomputed PRO-EDGE INPUTS.
pro_edge.script_read: Spread is 1.5, not 3.5+, so Jacksonville is not a forced pass-chase dog and there is no blowout flag on starter snaps. Total 47.5 is moderate: not a volume-over environment and not a low-total run rock fight. Lead-back carry bumps only if someone actually pulls away. Usage has to come from shares: Etienne 47 of JAX’s listed RB carries in the L3, Walker 45 of SEA’s.
pro_edge.best_price: None. Etienne rushyds 71.5, Etienne rushrecyds 89.5, Thomas recyds 49.5 and every other listed prop are saved as no two-sided price, no-vig N/A. No Pinnacle, Circa or BetOnline anchor, no power devig, no edge pts, no gate pts. Stake proposal withheld. Not a bet.
pro_edge.lagging: Cannot flag a lagging book. No open-to-close prop grid was saved, so the Jones/Hall outs and the doubtful cluster cannot be checked against a moved or unmoved number.
pro_edge.sleepers: OUT: Josh Jones (SEA T) and Derick Hall (SEA LB). No same-position teammate props exist to reprice. Beneficiaries if the number is stale: Walker efficiency down, JAX pass catchers up because Hall is out. DOUBTFUL, sleeper check incomplete until inactives: Love, Woolen, Witherspoon, Hainsey. QUESTIONABLE: Abdullah. If Woolen and Witherspoon are later ruled out, Thomas is the WR1 whose 49.5 median stand-in may lag; that diff cannot be run with no prices.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Etienne’s 71.5 rushing number is only his season-median stand-in, but Seattle allows 3.43 yards per carry and five 10-yard runs in five games, and Jacksonville center Robert Hainsey is doubtful, so today’s efficiency should finish under that median.
edge_players.must_be_true: Etienne keeps the lead-back share he has had (47 carries over weeks 3–5) in a one-score game, and the Seattle front plays like its 3.43 YPC profile. Hainsey sitting is a plus, not required.
edge_players.kills_it: Hainsey plays, Jacksonville leads, and Etienne gets a 20-carry grind, or he repeats the explosive game that produced 124 yards. A SEA-lead script helps the under, it does not kill it.

pre_mortem: It’s Monday and this lost because the 124 was a role trait, not a fluke: Seattle’s 3.43 YPC was built on other opponents, Hainsey played, Jacksonville led, and Etienne got 20 carries for 90-plus. Thomas lost because Woolen, Witherspoon and Love were all active, Seattle blitzed near 20%, and the 0.00 EPA in non-blitz looks showed up as checkdowns to Strange (15 targets, 128 yards L3) while Thomas sat on 49 again. Unsaved outdoor weather could also have cut the passing over without a forecast to lean on.
slip_story: One story only: Seattle’s run front and a doubtful Jacksonville center cap Etienne, while a short-handed Seattle secondary leaves Thomas as the outlet in a 24.5–23 game. They win together if the run is stuck and Jacksonville throws; they lose together if Jacksonville grinds. Do not add Walker over, a total under, or a TD. Candidate card only; pro-edge never bets.
